text:
Maria: Heads-up: performing private deployment hardening + KMS sync on Fri 02:00 UTC. This includes RBAC tightening, network policy lockdown, audit sink test, and a vuln-gate check before we flip any keys. Need owners for: netpol verification, RBAC manifest, audit forwarding, and incident rollback.

Kira: I can take RBAC manifests. Plan: create a scoped 'keystore-rotator' role with only Encrypt/ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey and bind to service accounts via k8s-svcaccount mapping. No wildcard ARNs. I'll stage in staging and run policy lint.

Sam: I'll own netpols. Important: we need to validate egress for HSM host ranges + any TLS termination proxies. Suggest a minimal policy with explicit ipBlock egress + allow to kube-dns and metadata. We should also test CNI-level conntrack settings (nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established) because long-lived TLS handshakes to HSM can span minutes.

Ben: Ops note  there's a low severity vuln in our TLS parser used by keystore-agent (CVE-2026-1122). Patch v1.4.5 is out but it changes ALPN ordering for compatibility. If we rotate keys before agents are rolled, some TLS sessions will be rejected. We must gate rotation on rolling patch status.

Trish: For audits: enable high-fidelity KMS audit events for the window and sample 100% of rewraps. Ship structured JSON to long-term bucket and to Splunk with field names: event, key_id, principal, pod, result, latency_ms. Add an audit-only webhook that also posts to an internal incident channel for any non-200 results.

infra-bot: PRE-CHECKS: (1) NTP drift < 2s for nodes + bastion + HSM; (2) RBAC manifest applied in staging and tokens tested; (3) Netpol smoke OK; (4) Keystore-agent version >= 1.4.5 in 90% of pods.

Maria: Good. For rollback triggers let's be explicit: revert if decrypt_fail_rate > 0.4% sustained for 3m OR keystore-proxy.auth_errors > 100 in 5m OR rewrap latency p50 spikes > 500ms and p95 > 2s. Reversion must be automated to update control-plane pointer back to previous key and revoke rotator creds.

Kira: RBAC manifest example (staged):
```
apiVersion: rbac.redwood/v1
kind: ServiceRole
metadata:
  name: keystore-rotator
spec:
  principals:
    - kind: ServiceAccount
      name: rotator-sa
  permissions:
    - action: kms:Encrypt
    - action: kms:ReEncrypt
    - action: kms:GenerateDataKey
  resource: arn:onprem:kms:east:key/rot-2026
  ttl_seconds: 300
```

Sam: Netpol smoke snippet will be in git. Extra note: if using eBPF dataplane, ensure policies don't accidentally block hostNetwork flows; test with an egress proxy container with same SA and simulate handshake.

Ben: Plan B if agents not patched: (A) do control-plane key promotion read-only (primary for encrypts, old key still for decrypts), (B) hold off tenant rewraps, (C) enable audit-only and rate-limit rewrap attempts. This minimizes impact while we finish rollout.

Trish: Observability: create temporary Grafana dashboard with kms.decrypt.success, kms.decrypt.fail, keystore-proxy.auth.fail, rewrap.attempts, rewrap.errors and add paging thresholds. Also create a Splunk query to extract non-OK audit events within 1m.

Maria: Incident response: on page, runbook steps: 1) Confirm metric spike and correlate with audit entries; 2) Trigger automated rollback job (if criteria met) or run manual revert; 3) Rotate/expire temporary rotator creds; 4) Open postmortem and tag affected tenants. Keep timeline metadata in the PM.

infra-bot: ACTIONS ASSIGNED: Kira -> rbac manifest + staging test; Sam -> netpols + conntrack test; Ben -> agent patch rollout plan + vuln gating; Trish -> audit sink + dashboards; Maria -> runbook + exec. Dry-run Wed 20:00 UTC.

Kira: One more RBAC item: ensure service account tokens are not mounted by default and use projected tokens with audience to limit scope. We'll update pod specs in canary before mass rollout.

Sam: Running IPv6 checks as well. Also will validate iptables conntrack table sizes in staging and increase if necessary to avoid evictions during the canary load.

Ben: I'll prepare a canary plan: 5% of traffic, then 25% after 10m if metrics stable, then full. Agents will include a compatibility flag to fallback to old ALPN ordering if TLS negotiation fails.

Trish: Forensics: capture raw TLS handshakes for failed attempts (SNI + chosen ciphers) in a debug buffer for 5m post-failure and rotate out after incident. Ship to secure S3 with restricted access.

Maria: Great. If dry-run is green, proceed with Friday cutover. Keep this channel for immediate updates; tag @pagerduty oncall if any blocking alerts. Thanks everyone.
